content.title: About
content.content: Plain baby toddler yogurt is a gentle dairy product made from whole cow's milk without added sugar, flavorings, or colorants. It contains live cultures of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium that support a healthy gut microbiome and is suitable for children from 6 months old.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The yogurt provides probiotics that help strengthen a child's immune system.
Plain yogurt is often one of the first dairy foods introduced when transitioning from breast milk to solid foods.
Unlike fruit‑flavored yogurts, plain versions contain no added sugar, making them kinder to young teeth.
The natural acidity of yogurt enhances calcium and phosphorus absorption.
Enzymes in yogurt partially break down lactose, making it easier to digest for children with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Live cultures promote the growth of beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and immunity.

items.title: Source of calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Calcium is essential for bone and tooth development, while vitamin D aids its absorption.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein supports muscle growth and overall development in toddlers.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugars helps avoid rapid blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Fermentation enzymes partially break down lactose, making the product more tolerable for children with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to casein or whey, causing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Kids with pronounced lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Shelf‑life monitoring
items.content: Yogurt spoils quickly if not stored properly; always consume before the printed date.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper handling after opening can allow pathogenic bacteria to grow.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve 50–100 ml portions from a clean spoon. It can be mixed with fruit or vegetable purees or stirred into oatmeal for variety. Do not add sugar or honey for children under one year.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 2–3 days and do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
